Publication bias table for a meta-analysis

Source: R/publication_bias.R
apa_publication_bias.Rd

Makes an APA-style table of tests and corrections for publication bias (small-study effects) in a meta-analysis fit with metafor::rma(), as computed by metafor.

Usage

apa_publication_bias(
  fit,
  methods = c("egger", "rank", "trimfill"),
  transform = TRUE
)

Arguments

fit

a meta-analysis fit with metafor::rma() (without moderators)

methods

methods to display, in order: any of "egger", "rank", "trimfill", and "fsn"

transform

if TRUE (default), estimates computed on a transformed scale are shown on their original scale, as in apa_parameters()

Value

apa7_tbl (tibble)

Details

The methods (rows) are:

  • "egger": Egger's regression test (metafor::regtest()), a meta-regression of the effect sizes on their standard errors. The test statistic is the test of the standard error's coefficient, and the adjusted estimate is the limit estimate (the predicted effect as the standard error approaches zero, as in PET).

  • "rank": Begg and Mazumdar's rank correlation test (metafor::ranktest()), Kendall's \(\tau\) between the standardized effect sizes and their variances.

  • "trimfill": the trim-and-fill method (metafor::trimfill()), which imputes the studies (\(k_0\)) that seem to be missing from one side of the funnel plot and gives the pooled estimate with them included.

  • "fsn": the fail-safe N (metafor::fsn()), the number of additional studies with an average effect of zero that would make the pooled estimate nonsignificant. It is widely criticized and is not shown by default.

Adjusted estimates are shown on the same scale as in apa_parameters() (e.g., risk ratios are exponentiated, and Fisher's z values are converted back to correlations), and apa_note() gives the unadjusted pooled estimate for comparison and describes each method.

These methods are available for models fit with metafor::rma(), not for multilevel models (metafor::rma.mv()), for which the standard error (or sampling variance) can be added as a moderator instead.

References

Begg, C. B., & Mazumdar, M. (1994). Operating characteristics of a rank correlation test for publication bias. Biometrics, 50(4), 1088–1101. doi:10.2307/2533446

Duval, S., & Tweedie, R. (2000). Trim and fill: A simple funnel-plot-based method of testing and adjusting for publication bias in meta-analysis. Biometrics, 56(2), 455–463. doi:10.1111/j.0006-341X.2000.00455.x

Egger, M., Davey Smith, G., Schneider, M., & Minder, C. (1997). Bias in meta-analysis detected by a simple, graphical test. BMJ, 315(7109), 629–634. doi:10.1136/bmj.315.7109.629

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("metafor", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("metadat", quietly = TRUE)) {
  d_bcg <- metafor::escalc(
    measure = "RR",
    ai = tpos, bi = tneg, ci = cpos, di = cneg,
    data = metadat::dat.bcg
  )
  fit_meta <- metafor::rma(yi, vi, data = d_bcg)
  apa_publication_bias(fit_meta)
}
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   Method                  Statistic Value `*p*` `Adjusted *RR*` `95% CI`      
#>   <chr>                   <chr>     <chr> <chr> <chr>           <chr>         
#> 1 Egger's regression test *z*       −0.80 ".42" "0.60"          "[0.33, 1.10]"
#> 2 Rank correlation test   *&tau;*     .03 ".95" ""              ""            
#> 3 Trim and fill           *k*~0~     1    ""    "0.52"          "[0.37, 0.74]"
# }
